description: Public MemoryStore.set_groups accepts an empty sequence; ChromaDB metadata merge would keep the old groups. The grow-only rule lives only in a comment.
DedupEntry and _NewItem keep kind and payload as separate fields, so mismatched pairs can be built.
_both_paths only asserts direct hits appear in the tool result, never that out-of-scope questions are absent.
No test covers set_groups raising MemoryChangedDuringImportError when a record disappears mid-import, on any surface.
No test asserts the CLI prints the CSV dropped-groups Warning:.
record_groups silently returns [] for a tagged record with malformed memory_groups, while scope_filter treats it as tagged; export then re-import makes it visible to every rule set.
dedup_entries skips unreadable rows without counting or logging them, so their duplicates are saved again.
When saving a new item fails, the duplicates already merged into it are still counted as updated or skipped duplicates, though their groups are lost; the failure itself still surfaces as isError.
import_bundle writes set_groups before the save loop; the 'Partial progress so far is intentionally lost' comment does not say the group changes already written stay after a systemic abort.

The dedup_entries docstring (and iter_all docstring, docs/internal/agent/memory.md) claims it covers the same rows iter_all turns into bundle items; it keeps a looser set. Capped at Suggestion by the behavior-inert prose cap.

set_groups reads metadata then writes the whole dict in a separate call; a hit_count/last_hit_date update made in between (track_usage on, no rule-set file) is overwritten. Only usage counters are lost.
Public MemoryStore.set_groups accepts an empty sequence, which Chroma's metadata merge silently ignores; only a comment enforces that groups only grow.
Only the DedupEntry docstring ties question to kind (it is empty for a schema_doc); no check enforces it.
